title: Euro stablecoins and their potential effect on sovereign bond markets
summary: This ECB Macroprudential Bulletin article explores how the growth of euro-denominated stablecoins could affect euro area sovereign bond markets. Euro stablecoins currently have a market capitalisation of approximately €450 million (January 2026), up from €50 million at the beginning of 2024, compared to US dollar stablecoins at approximately USD 300 billion. The article defines a 'pass-through rate' measuring how stablecoin demand influences sovereign bond holdings and examines how this effect varies based on issuer type (bank vs. EMI), reserve asset composition, and liquidity management preferences.
key_points: Euro-denominated stablecoin market capitalisation reached approximately €450 million as of January 2026, up from €50 million at the beginning of 2024
US dollar-denominated stablecoin market capitalisation stands at approximately USD 300 billion, illustrating the nascent stage of euro stablecoins

MiCAR requires euro-denominated e-money token (EMT) issuers to hold at least 30% (60% for significant issuers) of reserve assets with credit institutions, with the remainder in low-risk highly liquid instruments such as sovereign bonds
Pass-through rate from stablecoin demand to sovereign bond holdings depends on issuer type (credit institution vs. EMI), reserve composition, and liquidity management preferences
One major EU bank is already issuing a stablecoin, while twelve other large EU banks have formed a consortium to launch a shared euro-denominated stablecoin

Large stablecoins with significant euro area sovereign debt holdings would increase interlinkages between the crypto-asset ecosystem and traditional finance, amplifying potential spillover risk and contagion effects
EMI deposit requirements under MiCAR can act as a liquidity buffer during stress periods but could also transmit stablecoin run stress to the banking system
why_it_matters: Stablecoins are increasingly important in financial markets, and euro-denominated stablecoins could become meaningful participants in euro area sovereign bond markets as the sector grows. Understanding the pass-through mechanism is critical for assessing potential systemic risks, particularly how a large stablecoin run could transmit stress to traditional banking and sovereign debt markets. This analysis informs regulators and market participants about the evolving interconnections between crypto assets and conventional finance.
market_structure_context: The article is primarily focused on market structure, examining: (1) how stablecoin growth could affect sovereign bond market demand, (2) the role of issuer type (bank vs. EMI) in determining reserve asset composition, (3) the pass-through rate from stablecoin demand to sovereign bond holdings, (4) MiCAR regulatory requirements for reserve assets, (5) potential spillover risks between the crypto-asset ecosystem and traditional finance, and (6) the operational implications of deposit requirements for EMIs as potential liquidity buffers or stress transmitters.
important_numbers: USD 300 billion — US dollar-denominated stablecoin market cap
30% — minimum reserve assets required with credit institutions (standard EMT issuers)
60% — minimum reserve assets required with credit institutions (significant EMT issuers)
